slots.name: vm_commit
slots.description: Commits pages in a reserved virtual memory region. Flags 0 retain lazy commitment. vm_commit_flag_resident commits, zeroes and pins physical RAM before success, in calls of at most vm_commit_resident_max_bytes; pages stay pinned until decommit/release. Unsupported flags fail explicitly. On failure a partially committed region may remain and must be released; no I/O or reclaim wait occurs during commitment.

slots.name: vm_decommit

slots.name: vm_release

slots.description: R4SYS starts a generation-keyed program, task, and thread inventory snapshot without allocating kernel memory.

slots.name: program_inventory_programs
slots.description: R4SYS reads one mutation-safe program inventory page and returns an explicit restart status if the captured epochs changed.

slots.name: program_inventory_tasks
slots.description: R4SYS reads one mutation-safe task inventory page and returns an explicit restart status if the captured epochs changed.

slots.name: program_inventory_threads

slots.name: thread_create_handle
slots.description: R4SYS creates a joinable thread and returns its exact generation-safe identity. Flags accept zero or thread_create_flag_compute_worker; unknown bits or missing runtime.workers=owned-v1 return thread_error_unsupported. A compute caller passes its compute role to descendants even with zero flags. Foreground main scheduling and console ownership are unchanged; compute workers retain exact instance VM/resource and join/exit ownership.

slots.name: thread_handle_join
slots.description: R4SYS joins only the exact thread generation carried by a ProgramJoinHandle.

slots.name: thread_handle_status
slots.description: R4SYS queries only the exact thread generation carried by a ProgramJoinHandle.

slots.name: file_replace_atomic
slots.description: R4SYS transfers a staged FAT file into a target with a durable sibling backup and without a copy/delete fallback.

slots.name: file_delete_if_match
slots.description: R4SYS deletes a file only when its size, FNV-1a checksum and filesystem identity still match under one serialized filesystem gate.

slots.name: file_update_atomic_checked
slots.description: R4SYS completes or reverses one SYSUPD ownership transfer only after target, stage and backup fingerprints plus transient filesystem identities match a legitimate journal state under one serialized filesystem gate. The additive long_stage flag permits an existing FAT32 long-name stage for forward completion only; the backup and newly created target remain short names, and the stage short entry is durably detached before its LFN slots are reclaimed.

slots.name: path_names_equal_collated
slots.description: R4SYS reports whether two paths would resolve to the same object on their shared volume using the filesystem own collation (NTFS $UpCase, FAT32 ASCII case fold), so callers never mistake a byte-wise fold for identity.

slots.name: file_update_cleanup_checked
slots.description: R4SYS completes one SYSUPD per-payload cleanup with target, stage, current backup and previous backup bound together to expected identity, size and checksum under one serialized filesystem gate.

slots.name: file_stream_declare_publish
slots.description: R4SYS records the create-only publish intent of an already open stream, including which protocol owns it, so the durable claim brackets the whole transfer instead of only the final hand-over and recovery telemetry can attribute an abandoned stage to SFTP, SCP or FTP.

slots.name: module_resource_stat
slots.description: R4SYS resolves one embedded resource of an R4M0 module file by type plus index or name and returns its exact size without reading the payload.

slots.name: module_resource_read
slots.description: R4SYS reads one embedded resource of an R4M0 module file completely into a caller-owned buffer; a too small buffer is a visible error, never a silent truncation.

slots.name: program_module_path
slots.description: R4SYS writes the absolute module file path of the calling program into a caller-owned buffer, so a program can read its own embedded resources without a hardcoded second truth beside the manifest TARGET.

slots.name: program_module_running
slots.description: Returns one when a published R4X instance from the exact absolute module path is still running, zero when no such instance exists, and a negative program error when the query cannot be completed.

slots.name: monotonic_clock
slots.description: Reads the backend-stable monotonic nanosecond instant together with calibrated source and periodic-event metadata without reading the RTC.

slots.name: boot_ready
slots.description: Lets the active boot shell mark its first usable frame or prompt exactly once; repeated calls by that shell are idempotent.

slots.name: registry_snapshot_begin
slots.description: Starts a caller-owned, generation-keyed registry child-key or value snapshot without allocating kernel memory.

slots.name: registry_snapshot_page
slots.description: Reads one bounded registry snapshot page directly from the captured key range and reports restart instead of exposing mixed generations.

slots.name: registry_batch_mutate
slots.description: Validates and commits one bounded set/delete batch as a single registry generation with no partial visible mutation.

slots.name: io_file_write_at
slots.description: Starts an asynchronous, progress-reporting file write at an absolute byte offset without truncating unrelated data.

slots.name: io_file_info
slots.description: Starts an asynchronous metadata query; the terminal IoStatus result is the file size in bytes or an I/O error.

slots.name: io_file_lock
slots.description: Asynchronously acquires or exactly releases a caller-owned advisory byte-range lock; conflicts complete with io_error_lock_violation.

slots.name: storage_inventory
slots.description: Refresh newly registered devices and return a topology snapshot. All payloads are copied; no borrowed driver strings escape.

slots.name: storage_device
slots.description: Read one device slot from the exact inventory generation. Absent slots return zero.

slots.name: storage_partition
slots.description: Read one partition from the exact complete inventory; invalid or partial tables remain explicit.

slots.name: storage_volume
slots.description: Read one exact mounted-volume snapshot, including the internal boot alias.

slots.name: storage_claim_begin
slots.description: Reject stale, partial, protected or used targets before modification; close admissions, drain, flush and unmount, then return an exact logical-thread-owned exclusive claim. Failure returns no claim and performs no raw mutation.

slots.name: storage_claim_end
slots.description: Close raw admission, flush, rescan and remount prior identities unless KEEP_UNMOUNTED is set. A completed close consumes the claim even when I/O or remount fails; BUSY retains a finishing claim for retry. Failed targets remain visible.

slots.name: storage_read
slots.description: Read at most storage_raw_max_sectors from a complete validated target; concurrent exclusive claims return BUSY. The output buffer holds sectors times 512 bytes.

slots.name: storage_claim_read
slots.description: Perform bounded synchronous read within an active caller-owned claim. Buffer remains caller-owned for the call. An I/O error may follow partial hardware progress; never replay writes automatically.

slots.name: storage_claim_write
slots.description: Perform bounded synchronous write within an active caller-owned claim. Buffer remains caller-owned for the call. An I/O error may follow partial hardware progress; never replay writes automatically.

slots.name: storage_claim_flush
slots.description: Issue the durability barrier for an active caller-owned claim and report backend failure.

slots.name: storage_rescan
slots.description: Acquire the complete device, drain/unmount, reread its table and remount matching previous identities. Open uses reject rescan before unmount.

slots.name: storage_mount
slots.description: Probe and mount a complete partition with a fresh generation. Letter zero assigns the first free D through Z except reserved R; C and R cannot be reassigned through this call.

slots.name: storage_unmount
slots.description: Drain and unmount the selected physical volume and its aliases. Required runtime volumes and open uses reject the operation.

slots.name: storage_use_begin
slots.description: Acquire a real physical-volume use lease for a resolved path, including the system boot alias. File and directory handles hold this lease until close or logical owner retirement.

slots.name: storage_use_end
slots.description: Release an exact caller-owned volume use lease; stale or foreign identifiers are rejected.

slots.name: directory_change_begin
slots.description: Capture a directory identity and current change sequence under the filesystem request gate. Returns 0 on success, -1 for invalid cursor/path, -3 for missing mount/directory, -9 for an I/O failure. Register before the initial enumeration.

slots.name: directory_change_poll
slots.description: Consume RAM-only changes for the captured directory. Returns 1 if a reload is needed (also on bounded history overflow), 0 if unchanged, -1 for invalid cursor, -3 for a retired mount. Mutations wake desktop_activity_wait. No persistent allocation and no close.

slots.name: file_copy_buffered
slots.description: Copies under one paired filesystem request, rejecting source aliases before destination mutation. Caller exclusively owns the supplied nonempty buffer until return. File-stream result codes: 0 success, invalid for identical files, too_large above 4 GB, I/O on failure. Progress reports completed appends; failure may leave a partial target. No automatic retry or rollback.

slots.name: notification_create
slots.description: Create a resident process-owned notification with revision zero. Handles never repeat within a boot. Returns notification status; output changes only on success. Allocation failure is explicit. Close explicitly or let exact process retirement reclaim it.

slots.name: notification_query
slots.description: Read the notification revision. Read before testing the userland predicate, then wait with that revision to avoid a lost wake. Foreign or consumed handles are stale; output changes only on success.

slots.name: notification_notify
slots.description: Increment the revision and wake at most wake_count enrolled tasks atomically. Count must be positive; UINT32_MAX broadcasts. A caller racing enrollment observes the changed revision. No permit, CPU-memory ownership or GPU completion is manufactured. Revision exhaustion closes the object and wakes all with closed.

slots.name: notification_wait
slots.description: Wait only while the resident revision equals observed_sequence. Zero polls; UINT64_MAX waits indefinitely. Predicate check, scheduler enrollment and notify share one owner. Returns 0 on change/wake, 1 on timeout, negative on failure/close; caller must recheck its own predicate. Close cancels enrolled waits. Hard kill detaches the actual task node and needs no caller destructor. No caller address or unwind guard is retained across sleep.

slots.name: notification_close
slots.description: Close admission, cancel enrolled waits and release resident backing. Returns 0 after release; retry notification_error_release for the same closed handle. A failed free retains backing and prevents process-slot reuse. Further ordinary operations on a closed retained object fail; a consumed handle is stale.

slots.name: program_local_get
slots.description: Read a process-local immutable publication by nonzero key. Returns program_local_ok and zero if absent. A key can be a boot-stable library token address. Output changes only on success. No other process, user pointer ownership or current-thread identity is exposed.

slots.name: program_local_publish
slots.description: Publish a nonzero process-local value exactly once for a nonzero key. Returns program_local_ok if installed, program_local_existing if another caller already installed a value; both write the winning value. Caller owns candidate memory and discards it when it loses. Published data must outlive all program threads; no replacement, destructor or allocator policy is provided. The process reaper removes metadata after thread retirement and before VM teardown. Errors leave output unchanged.

slots.name: thread_current_handle
slots.description: Copy the calling program thread identity, including thread and process generations, into ProgramJoinHandle. Returns thread_ok on success, thread_error_no_instance outside a program thread, or thread_error_invalid for a null output. Errors leave output unchanged. The identity is borrowed: no pin, join lease, allocation or wait is created; normal status/join admission and retirement rules still apply. Lookup uses the current task execution owner and never scans a registry. Valid for the main thread as well as secondary threads.

slots.name: cpu_capacity
slots.description: Copy current schedulable CPU capacity for ordinary program threads. Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid for null output, or thread_error_busy before capacity is available; errors leave output unchanged. available_cpus counts one atomic scheduler-admission mask snapshot (no process affinity restrictions currently exist). configured_cpus counts dense CPU slots admitted by the boot SMP plan, including failed/offline slots; it is not the CPUID package count, firmware total or kernel maximum. Capacity is advisory, not a reservation, affinity mask, cache topology or performance guarantee. No allocation or wait.

slots.name: program_exit
slots.description: Terminates the entire calling program from its main or a secondary thread. On admission this does not return. reason accepts program_exit_reason_natural or program_exit_reason_failed only; invalid reason returns thread_error_invalid, missing program-thread ownership returns thread_error_no_instance, and a non-sleepable context or held kernel lock/unwind lifetime returns thread_error_busy without initiating exit. The first committed concurrent process exit wins. The existing exit/reaper path closes admission, stops peers and retains stacks, I/O and graphics resources through actual retirement; the caller transfers its own terminal Task to the scheduler reaper. Does not run user destructors, atexit, TLS callbacks, stream flushing or foreign stack unwinding; normal userland shutdown precedes this primitive, fatal shutdown may omit it. External kill still rejects self. Older providers may omit this optional tail.

slots.name: platform_input_snapshot
slots.description: Copy the canonical ACPI/USB Consumer input snapshot without consuming events.1 success, negative invalid output. Caller initializes version1/size64; output unchanged on failure. No hardware access, callback or allocation. Desktop policy observes counter deltas and lid state independently from normal keyboard text.

slots.name: directory_next
slots.description: Resume owner-bound directory enumeration without prefix scans. Initialize DirectoryScanCursor to defaults. Returns 0 file, 1 directory, 2 bounded progress without an entry (retry), -5 complete EOF, -10 restart after directory mutation, history overflow, owner/path/mount change; other negatives are errors (-1 invalid, -3 missing mount, -7 output too small, -9 I/O). On restart/error discard all partial results; no truncated successful generation. Cursor and output are unchanged on errors; progress and EOF publish cursor only. Success copies a NUL-terminated absolute path. One call examines at most 256 physical directory entries, with a bounded NTFS ancestor stack. Internal state is opaque, must not be edited or used concurrently. No persistent kernel resource, allocation or mount pin; discarding/resetting cursor cancels/closes immediately. A call pins its mount and holds the filesystem request gate; an unmount between calls invalidates continuation. Old dir_entry ABI remains unchanged. A found entry also copies FileInfo metadata from the same enumeration record; no second name lookup. NTFS directory-index metadata has the same snapshot semantics as its index entry. On progress, EOF or failure metadata is unchanged.

slots.name: thread_placement_get
slots.description: Get placement of the exact live thread/instance generations (including main). Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid/no_instance/not_found/busy or thread_placement_error_capacity. Validate info version1 and capacity>=64. word_capacity0 allows null cpus and returns metadata including required word count; otherwise capacity must suffice and cpus must be nonnull. Copy exactly cpu_word_count words and64 info bytes on success; all outputs and tails unchanged on errors. Caller buffers must not overlap. No allocation or retained caller pointer.

slots.name: thread_placement_set
slots.description: Set placement of an exact live thread/instance generation (including main). Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid/no_instance/not_found/busy/unsupported or thread_placement_error_capacity. Reject unknown flags/class/reserved data, empty sets, unavailable or module-disallowed CPUs and hints outside the set, without state changes. Explicit input length must equal the discovered required word count; default-cpus requires word_count0. Running acceptance may remain pending until full outgoing RSP/FPU save; query revisions. No synchronous wait or realtime guarantee. Repeated equal requests do not renew preferred-class budgets; class toggles share one bounded activation budget. No retained caller pointer.

slots.name: system_power_transition
slots.description: Explicit bounded blocking orderly system transition: power_transition_action_halt/reboot/poweroff. Closes new CPU control ownership and pins current CPU membership before cooperative POWERSVC stop and real same-CPU request return. No Runtime owner over waits. Refusal returns a negative power_transition_error_* and retains real resources without stopping APs; CPU ownership reopens. Accepted transition becomes terminal and does not return. Missing/disabled provider stays functional. Existing nonblocking raw system_halt/reboot/poweroff slots retain their signatures/meanings; with held requests they refuse immediately rather than waiting or falsely acknowledging return. Profiles/parameter policy stay external. timeout_ticks is an explicit wait budget, clamped to5 seconds;0 requests only a bounded poll. Timeout/refusal may follow an already requested cooperative service stop; query status rather than automatic retry. The immediate legacy slots never perform this new service wait.

slots.name: entropy_source_info
slots.description: Purely cached registered-device source observation. Original source/driver epoch and module generation retained after close. No callback/device/CPU instruction, I/O or entropy consumption.

slots.name: entropy_fill
slots.description: Explicit bounded registered-device source read,1..4096bytes. Ordinary task with IF on, exact task admission through output, exact driver instance/lifecycle lease through resident callback/staging, no Runtime owner over wait. Release driver owner before potentially paged caller copy. Positive exact count only with confirmed full receipt; failure discards/clears valid caller range, never initial/partial entropy. No RNG pool or clock/ID substitute; SDK owns RDRAND-first/source choice.

slots.name: program_lifecycle_begin
slots.description: Nonblocking process-registry epoch admission only. Initializes the existing cursor with initialized|lifecycle, snapshot_generation=program_epoch, no registry traversal, allocation, VM, heap, task or thread diagnostics. Failure leaves cursor unchanged; Busy is not lifecycle authority. Does not cache or equate program epochs with all mutable metadata.

slots.name: program_lifecycle_programs
slots.description: One bounded generation-ordered lifecycle page from the canonical process registry, including pending/done completions. Forty-byte records carry exact handles and current process fields without VM statistics. Epoch mismatch returns restart with no row/cursor advancement; Busy/invalid has no complete authority. Complete paging must finish before adoption/disappearance decisions; revalidate exact handles at actions. A lifecycle cursor cannot be used by full inventory calls or vice versa.

slots.name: drive_info_geometry
slots.description: Returns the same mounted drive identity/capacity and scalar cluster geometry without executing FREE or reading a free-space bitmap. Existing exact mount/request admission can wait. Free fields and drive_info_flag_free_valid are zero: explicitly unknown, not measured zero. Existing DriveInfo56 layout unchanged. index0..25; returns1 mounted,0 unmounted,-1 invalid index,-2 request unavailable.

slots.name: directory_batch
slots.description: Initialize with path and default2160-byte cursor; continuation uses its captured node/path with exact logical-owner, mount and mutation validation. Return1..capacity complete1120-byte records,0 bounded progress,-5 EOF; -1 invalid,-3 absent/not-directory initially,-7 full-path bounds,-9 I/O/admission,-10 stale/foreign/cancel. Capacity1..8; one shared256-step backend budget and prepared metadata per visit. Initialized capacity0/out=NULL validates without advancing (RAM-only while namespace unchanged); input path is ignored on continuation. No persistent kernel allocation/scan lease; call guards always release, including caller unwind. Outputs/cursor have no authority on error. A caller must not modify or concurrently reuse a cursor.

slots.name: program_observation_retain
slots.description: Create an independent observation binding to the exact process handle and generation while its completion record still exists. Once the last retaining reference is released and the consumed record is removed, retain fails; it never reconstructs missing completion or output evidence. flags0 binds cleanup to the calling process generation; PORTABLE explicitly survives creator exit until release. Returns copied row count, END explicitly proves EOF, DYNAMIC reports no compiled count limit. Membership/configuration changes return RESTART; callers discard all partial pages. Cursor/rows remain unchanged on errors; buffer tail remains untouched. capacity must be positive and only bounds one transfer; arbitrary many pages are supported. Complete 1024-byte paths and exact registration/start/process bindings are returned. Runtime and endpoint counters are per-owner observations. No new process/endpoint lease is granted.

slots.name: service_control_bound
slots.description: Apply START/STOP/RESTART/MODE/REMOVE only to the original registration ID and expected full process/start binding. Uses existing native generation-aware start/stop/reap, absolute stop deadline, restart/disable and self-restart policy. MODE requires a valid public mode; other operations require mode0. Original one Task wait_node enrolls only in resident set queue. Source publications and enrollment are atomic; close/kill detach real links. slots.name: waitset_close

Already removed handles are stale; SDK owner may make its own completed close idempotent.

slots.name: byte_pipe_read

Cancel/close wakes actual waiters; every wake re-resolves full endpoint identity. Last writer close then drain yields EOF; last reader close yields BrokenPipe with zero accepted bytes. slots.description: Copies one immutable committed GUI frame into caller-owned command and resource buffers in one generation-checked operation. The handle is mandatory. Null payload pointers require zero capacity. GuiFrameInfo version 1 or newer with size at least 176 is accepted and answered as the supported v1/176 prefix. Version zero or a smaller size modifies neither out_info nor either payload buffer and returns gui_frame_error_invalid. On stale, buffer-too-small or other invalid input neither payload buffer is modified; out_info remains valid and reports the current owner, generation and required counts.

slots.name: display_blit_xrgb32_stride
slots.description: Copies an XRGB32 source rectangle with an explicit source row stride into the display frame. source_stride_pixels must be at least w and pixel_count must cover the last addressed pixel.

slots.name: display_present_regions
slots.description: Presents one XRGB32 source generation through the canonical bounded multi-region path and returns its synchronous fence and selected backend.

slots.name: display_present_capabilities
slots.description: Returns the active canonical present backend, exact damage limits, formats and CPU fallback capabilities.

slots.name: display_present_completion
slots.description: Polls completion of a canonical present fence. The current bootframebuffer and external blit backends complete synchronously.

slots.name: gui_frame_begin_damage
slots.description: Begins a private transactional GUI delta frame for the current GUI program. The bounded client-local regions are copied during the call and describe every pixel that the appended commands may change. A successful commit retains the previous immutable generation as its base without cloning it.

slots.name: gui_frame_generation_info
slots.description: Returns exact local counts, base generation, damage regions and telemetry for one immutable generation in the current committed chain. The generation must be nonzero and the process handle is mandatory.

slots.name: gui_frame_generation_read
slots.description: Copies only the commands, resources and exact client-local damage regions owned by one immutable generation. Resource offsets remain local to the returned blob. On stale, buffer-too-small or invalid input no payload buffer is modified and out_info reports the generation requirements when available.

slots.name: font_glyph_bitmap
slots.description: Copies one complete cached monochrome glyph, including its metrics and least-significant-bit-first row masks, after resolving the glyph exactly once. Missing glyphs use the same built-in fallback as the existing font renderer.

slots.name: font_revision
slots.description: Returns the non-zero generation of the live system-font catalogue. Every completed catalogue reload advances the generation so consumers can invalidate font-id keyed caches even when ids or metadata are reused.

slots.name: gui_frame_begin_replace
slots.description: Begins a private transactional complete replacement GUI frame for the current GUI program. The bounded client-local regions are copied during the call and describe every pixel changed from the prior generation. A successful commit publishes a standalone complete generation and supersedes the prior committed chain without retaining it as a base.

slots.name: gui_frame_stream_info
slots.description: Returns bounded replacement-stream lifecycle and native XRGB32 transport counters for one GUI program. The process handle is mandatory and invalid caller headers remain unchanged.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_create
slots.description: Creates one producer-owned bounded shared raster with three reusable backing buffers. The returned generation-exact handle is destroyed explicitly or automatically at producer exit.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_destroy
slots.description: Closes one exact producer-owned shared raster. Existing immutable frame and consumer references remain valid until their final release; no new write mapping is accepted.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_map_write
slots.description: Reserves one currently unreferenced backing buffer and returns its direct producer-writable address and an unforgeable write token. The mapping becomes immutable when published.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_publish
slots.description: Publishes one exact write mapping as a new immutable raster generation. The generation may be referenced by a standalone full or replacement GUI frame until its backing buffer is reused.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_acquire
slots.description: Acquires one immutable shared raster generation referenced by the exact captured GUI frame generation and returns the direct consumer mapping plus an explicit lease.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_release
slots.description: Releases one exact consumer lease. A stale, foreign or duplicate lease is rejected without changing shared-raster ownership.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_create
slots.description: Creates zeroed resident system RAM with checked descriptor and finite budget. Success is 1; failure leaves outputs untouched and retains any failed VM rollback internally.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_describe
slots.description: Copies the descriptor for one reference owned by the current caller.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_import
slots.description: Imports a live shareable reference into the current caller, preserving immutable mode. Producer exit closes new imports; existing references survive.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_release
slots.description: Drops one caller reference; maps, device jobs and scanout retain their own leases. Stale or duplicate release has no effect.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_map
slots.description: Retains a CPU read (0) or write (1) map with an explicit 64-bit range. Conflicting consumers return Busy; WC reads and unavailable CPU mappings are unsupported.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_unmap
slots.description: Ends one caller CPU map after the caller has stopped accessing it, orders CPU visibility, and permits deferred release. Device completion is not exposed through this function.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_export_raster
slots.description: Exports an exact held shared-raster consumer lease as an immutable BO reference without a pixel copy. The producer may not overwrite the buffer while that reference survives.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_stats
slots.description: Copies one coherent budget, object, reference and lease snapshot.

slots.name: gfx_queue_open
slots.description: Opens one bounded asynchronous queue for the current program. Unknown adapters or milestones return unsupported; no silent fallback.

slots.name: gfx_queue_close
slots.description: Closes the caller queue, cancels every pending fence, and drops caller fence references. Physical device uses survive until acknowledged quiescent.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit
slots.description: Returns after acceptance without executing commands or copying pixels. All descriptors and up to eight dependencies are copied; source/target leases retain backing and prevent premature CPU reuse. Failure leaves output and existing latest-frame work untouched.

slots.name: gfx_fence_query
slots.description: Snapshots one exact fence without waiting. A terminal cancellation may still report device-active; resources are reusable only after physical quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_fence_wait
slots.description: Waits without spinning or holding a metadata owner. timeout_ticks is a scheduler-tick duration, with UINT64_MAX meaning indefinite; the submission deadline remains independently finite in monotonic nanoseconds. Wait timeout leaves output unchanged and does not cancel the job. wait_for=0 waits for logical completion; wait_for=1 waits until the operation is physically quiescent and every queue BO lease has been released. Both events are sticky and generation-retained.

slots.name: gfx_fence_cancel
slots.description: Requests the sole logical cancelled completion for a caller-owned fence. Already terminal returns already-completed. Never asserts native DMA quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_fence_release
slots.description: Drops the caller fence reference. Active backing, dependency edges, wake publication and task-generation waiter records prohibit premature slot reuse.

slots.name: gfx_queue_backend
slots.description: Queries one fixed backend inventory slot, from zero through gfx_queue_backend_capacity minus one. Zero is software; other slots may be vacant. Returns 1 with an exact binding, 0 for vacant, negative for error; output changes only on 1. Revalidate by opening with the returned generations. No hidden fallback or successful partial enumeration.

slots.name: gfx_output_revision
slots.description: Reads the output revision used with existing desktop activity waits. No second event queue and no busy polling are required.

slots.name: gfx_output_info
slots.description: Reads one of the advertised fixed catalog slots; holes return zero without modifying output. Stable ports survive disconnects, receiver generations do not.

slots.name: gfx_output_mode
slots.description: Reads one source-filtered mode for an exact receiver incarnation. Stale never returns data belonging to a different receiver.

slots.name: gfx_output_edid
slots.description: Copies one complete raw EDID block for an exact receiver incarnation. Missing blocks return zero; invalid/stale leaves output unchanged.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_test
slots.description: Checks the complete output/geometry/format/pitch/PLL/plane/bandwidth/fence state without reservations or device writes. Native commits remain unsupported until hardware and all desktop consumers negotiate the full pipeline.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_commit
slots.description: Revalidates the complete state before committing. Currently the firmware backend only supports retaining its actual fixed scanout. Unnegotiated native mode/puffer changes return unsupported before any hardware write. Commit outcomes never imply VBlank.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_submit
slots.description: Submit an asynchronous single-primary native atomic change. Copies the complete state and retains full source references before returning. Requires an opted-in native backend and a 1000..60000 ms confirmation interval. Returns queued status, never a hardware success. Unsupported geometry or unavailable capability has no device effects.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_status
slots.description: Read the retained mode transaction without waiting. Ticket zero reads the latest transaction for diagnostics; an explicit obsolete ticket returns stale. Reading is allowed across caller exit and hardware loss.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_resolve
slots.description: The submitting program confirms the visible candidate or requests rollback. Confirmation is accepted only before its deadline. Cancellation and timeout are requests for actual driver rollback; backing remains retained until real completion. Status is nonblocking; caller exit does not stop the deadline worker.

slots.name: display_presentation_stats
slots.description: Read coherent per-head statistics from the current native primary backend. Returns gfx_output_ok or a negative gfx_output error, with no output mutation on failure. No waits, device calls or CPU-copy fence reinterpretation. Unsupported/boot framebuffer backends have no visible hardware completion sample.

slots.name: display_cursor_info
slots.description: Read optional native primary hardware-cursor capabilities. Unsupported leaves caller output unchanged.

slots.name: display_cursor_submit
slots.description: Submit one finite asynchronous cursor operation for the calling program. Busy keeps prior state. Prepare borrows the source until terminal completion; only successful show/hide confirmation changes visible ownership.

slots.name: display_cursor_status
slots.description: Read coherent primary cursor status without rendering or waits. A caller must not draw software while hardware visibility is confirmed or unknown.

slots.name: gfx_queue_backend_info
slots.description: Queries one existing backend inventory slot with its coherent optional protocol profile. Same 1/0/negative result and capacity as gfx_queue_backend; output changes only on 1. Profile bytes belong to the driver and are interpreted by the matching userland library, never by the kernel. Opening the exact returned binding detects reset or replacement.

slots.name: gfx_native_start
slots.description: Start a caller-owned native BO allocation. Copies input and returns a pending request. Exact provider memory generation and finite deadline required; at most 16 requests per program. No R4D callback executes on the application task. Receive or close each successful request; error leaves output unchanged.

slots.name: gfx_native_query
slots.description: Inspect a request owned by the current program. Logical terminal status does not prove physical driver cleanup. Output changes only on success.

slots.name: gfx_native_receive
slots.description: Atomically transfer a successful request-held BO reference to the current program and consume the request. Pending reports busy, failed returns its recorded error. Capacity failure leaves request available for retry. Output changes only on success.

slots.name: gfx_native_close
slots.description: Close a caller-owned allocation request; discard unreceived result and cancel queued work. Claimed work, provider callback and enrolled waiters remain retained until their exact completion. Cannot imply GPU or firmware quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_native_wait
slots.description: Wait on sticky request completion outside owner locks. Exact task-generation wait record survives hard task termination until reaper detach. Relative wait timeout leaves the request and output unchanged; allocation deadline separately closes logical work. Returns terminal status on 1, including failed/cancelled result.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_render_list
slots.description: Atomically admit 1..16 ordered draws with one retained source/target pair and one fence. Requires render_list operation6 and backend bit6; the ordinary submit entry rejects this operation. All list contents are copied before admission. No pixels or device command words are accepted.

slots.name: display_presentation_info
slots.description: Reports per-head presentation policy, real capabilities and scanout observations. Software copy reports no VSync or visibility guarantee. Caller initializes version1/size; output changes only on success.

slots.name: display_presentation_feedback
slots.description: Read one actual visible receipt by exact head and source queue fence from the bounded32-frame display history. Independent of current frame and queue-client release. No match returns unavailable; reset/takeover invalidates old history. A retained history record is metadata only, not a BO reference. released_ns retains its existing meaning: retirement of that flip previous image, not the submitted source.

slots.name: display_output_target
slots.description: Read the current exact presentation identity for one adapter/head. No match is unavailable; receiver-only catalog entries are not active presentation targets. Caller initializes version1/size48; changes output only on success. Adapter0 names the firmware/software adapter, never an implicit wildcard.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_output
slots.description: Present a complete image to an exact copied output target. Accepts only present/direct_present; validates all output generations and holds the same queue/BO lifetime as ordinary submission. Target selection is never silently reduced to the primary on older kernels: the separate optional slot is mandatory. Other outputs remain independent.

slots.name: display_output_presentation_info
slots.description: Read presentation capabilities for an exact copied GfxOutputTarget. Adapter/head and every generation must match. Success-only output; no primary fallback for stale or unknown targets.

slots.name: display_output_presentation_feedback
slots.description: Read one source fence visibility receipt from the exact output. No other adapter or head can satisfy the query; feedback retains the existing independently retired source lifetime.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_render_grid_list
slots.description: Copy one bounded draw/grid list to an admitted native queue. Operation render_grid_list is explicitly negotiated. Exact grid sampling stays in the R4D/GPU; common code retains source, target and immutable descriptors until the actual receipt.

slots.name: gfx_output_color
slots.description: Reads driver-published color capabilities and confirmed output encoding for the exact output identity. Missing source metadata returns unsupported; stale output never returns another receiver state. No hardware access or color conversion.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_render_color_list
slots.description: Submit1..16 compatible sampled draws and a copied bounded userland color program. Requires operation render_color_list. Coefficients, source and target remain retained until native completion; no partial list is admitted.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_test_color
slots.description: Validate one color mode request and its two distinct BOs against copied source facts without starting device work. Actual receiver/link/source revalidation still occurs in the native driver before commit.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_submit_color
slots.description: Submit a color mode request through the existing confirmation/rollback owner. Retains canonical SDR shadow plus separate encoded image and immutable signal; current active output color changes only after actual driver acknowledgement.

slots.name: gfx_output_refresh
slots.description: Read independent VRR capability, acknowledged state and actual hardware interval history for this exact output/mode. Missing implementation returns unsupported; output is untouched on error.

slots.name: gfx_refresh_request
slots.description: Set or renew bounded presenter VRR intent. Caller owns the intent until release, close or lease expiry. Returns assigned sequence/deadline without asserting that hardware has switched. Exact target required; operation is atomic on success.

slots.name: gfx_memory_budget
slots.description: Query the configured budget and retained BO charges of one exact adapter/memory generation. Read-only; configure operations are rejected. No R4D callback, allocation or hardware query. Error leaves output unchanged.

slots.name: gfx_telemetry
slots.description: Query one exact adapter/memory-generation telemetry snapshot and optionally renew finite demand. Pure metadata exchange with the existing R4D worker. No hardware access or callback. Unknown/expired measurements remain explicit; error preserves output.

slots.name: gfx_output_power
slots.description: Read acknowledged screen power and independent signal/sink capabilities. Firmware framebuffer and missing drivers return unsupported. Exact connector identity remains queryable while sleeping; output is unchanged on error.

slots.name: gfx_power_request
slots.description: Request or renew screen sleep, or wake immediately. Atomic copied intent with30s off lease; caller close and expiry wake. No GPU/system suspend or synchronous hardware operation. Driver acknowledgement is read separately.

slots.name: gfx_virtual_start
slots.description: Copy and admit an owner-bound GPU range or binding. Output changes only on success; a pending handle is not proof of completed hardware work. Finite creation deadline and exact adapter generation are required.

slots.name: gfx_virtual_query
slots.description: Read the exact caller resource, including after retirement requested with close mode 0. Never infer GPU quiescence from the creation result.

slots.name: gfx_virtual_close
slots.description: Mode 0 requests resource retirement while retaining the public handle for query/wait; mode 1 additionally releases that handle. Range close propagates to all bindings. Neither mode waits for GPU quiescence or discards an outstanding driver claim.

slots.name: gfx_virtual_wait
slots.description: Until 0 waits for settled creation, until 1 for confirmed backend retirement. Completion wins a concurrent wait timeout. A wait timeout changes neither the resource deadline nor its ownership. Exact task retirement removes waiter metadata.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_map_persistent
slots.description: Retain a persistent CPU read (0) or read/write (1) mapping of write-back system RAM. This lease holds backing, not exclusive execution access: device/queue uses may coexist. The caller must synchronize all CPU/GPU access and the driver must perform GPU cache/engine barriers. No GPU completion or host-coherent device capability is implied. Ordinary CPU maps, immutable exports and scanout retain their conflict rules. Close through gfx_buffer_unmap; exact process retirement removes this CPU lease while independent device uses continue to retain backing. Unsupported for VRAM, WC/UC or absent CPU backing.

slots.name: gfx_queue_backend_properties
slots.description: Read immutable vendor properties for an exact backend binding. Returns 1 on success, 0 when this live incarnation has no properties, negative for invalid/stale/lost/unsupported binding. Full output required; output unchanged on every non-success. Properties are hardware/protocol facts, not admitted queue operations or Vulkan feature qualification.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_native
slots.description: Submit native command metadata with the ordinary queue fence/dependency/deadline contract. operation must be native; all ordinary source/target/render/row fields must be empty. Backend native operation and exact profile identity required. Copies payload and binding array; reserves acknowledged mappings and canonical BO execution under the common owner. Close/cancel/producer exit cannot free active GPU resources; physical completion or proved reset is required. Driver validates private payload. Output unchanged on failure; no Linux ioctl or vendor method interpretation in the kernel.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_render_color_grid_list
slots.description: Atomically submit1..16 compatible color draws with per-draw logical grids. Requires render_color_grid_list capability. Copies all descriptors before entering the queue owner; no pixel conversion, intermediate image or partial submission.

slots.name: gfx_output_brightness
slots.description: Read the last driver brightness receipt. Output unchanged on failure; unavailable is explicit. current is confirmed programmed intensity, not measured luminance.

slots.name: gfx_brightness_request
slots.description: Admit a normalized brightness request for an exact native output generation. Latest writer wins, survives caller exit. Returns an admission serial only; hardware completion/failure is read separately. No synchronous hardware call.

slots.name: font_prefix_metrics2
slots.description: Bounded linear scalar-prefix widths under one existing exact font bank/task-unwind lease. Strict UTF8/no embedded NUL, explicit length0..4096, rows capacity0..4096. One preflight validates/counts; one emission pass uses current additive glyph advances and existing CR/LF maximum-line width behavior. Returns0 complete with unique nonzero bank revision/count/complete flag; -7 capacity reports required_count with no usable rows; all other errors grant no output authority. Empty source/capacity0 is a constant-work checked font stamp probe, no full text scan. Caller keeps immutable source and whole aligned disjoint exclusive outputs/code through real synchronous return. No heap, global text cache, persistent handle, second font owner, rendering/shaping/kerning or current-font/physical completion promise. Canonical font revision wrap permanently refuses new metrics rather than reusing identities; existing font APIs remain unchanged.

slots.name: audio_select_output
slots.description: Selects a NUL-terminated physical output identity in a 64-byte buffer. AUDSVC owns normal user selection; queued application streams and master volume survive the route switch.

slots.name: audio_stream_progress
slots.description: Returns canonical source/device progress for one owned stream generation; generation0 only binds a freshly opened stream. No speaker-emission receipt.

slots.name: audio_set_stream_expectation

slots.name: audio_close_stream_progress

slots.name: audio_output_catalog
slots.description: Copy the complete current output catalog in linear row-query work. Caller supplies at least256 AudioOutputInfo slots and a disjoint v1/size>=224 AudioOutputCatalog; no allocation or retained pointer. Returns1 on complete success, service_api_result_busy for contention/provider epoch change, err_no_fn if a registered provider lacks the epoch contract, invalid for malformed metadata/capacity. Metadata and buffer tail remain unchanged on failure; the row prefix is scratch and MUST be discarded unless result1. Count<=256; each provider count<=32, validated with its actual epoch before and after all rows under one registry permit. No retry loop, wait callback, hardware scan, route/Stop/ELD receipt or global availability lease. Scalar audio_output_info stays available for individual consumers.

slots.name: audio_capture_io
slots.description: Optional infrastructure-only nonblocking copied input backend IO through original R4D audio registry/permit. No kernel capture queue or decoder. Request and reply records are disjoint borrowed pointers; output PCM scratch is at most2048bytes/whole frames. Returns0 for a complete reply whose result carries operation outcome; negative mechanism errors do not publish reply metadata. No registered input returns explicit UnsupportedCapture in copied reply. R4D retains DMA/pins through failed Stop/Close/shutdown; input record is removed only after genuine hardware quiescence ACK. AUDSVC owns normal client catalog/queue/policy; no playback readback.

slots.name: driver_module_info
slots.description: Copies retained metadata of the initialized R4D owner; no file, PCI or MMIO reads. Returns 1 on success, 0 for no runtime R4D, -1 for invalid capacity/version/owner, -2 while the lifecycle is busy. No output on failure. Firmware version names the declared embedded bundle, never successful device execution.

slots.name: performance_instrumentation
slots.description: Reads instrumentation mode, sampling rates, enumeration bounds and clock quality without collecting the broad performance summary. Returns 1 on success, -1 for invalid version/capacity; no output on failure.

slots.name: performance_lock

slots.name: performance_stack
slots.description: Read-only resident instrumentation snapshot. Returns 1 on success, 0 beyond the index range, -1 for invalid version/capacity; no output on failure.

slots.name: stack_fault
slots.description: Read the latest resident stack failure for CPU slot index. Returns 1 for a coherent snapshot (sequence zero means no recorded failure), 0 beyond CPU slots, -1 for invalid version/capacity and -2 for a concurrently changing record after three attempts. Failure never changes output. No allocation, owner acquisition, scan, wait, trace activation or state reset.

slots.name: memory_kernel_heap_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded kernel-heap check after boot. Runs the existing allocator, patterns, alignment, double-free, 2000-op churn, 16-iteration acceptance and resident-commit cases with exact owned cleanup. Never assumes the global heap is empty and never resets global counters. Returns 1 for a versioned report (including failed, busy or cancelled), 0 when unavailable and -1 for invalid version/capacity without changing output. At most one check runs; normal heap users remain admitted. Close is cooperative; caller task lifetime is retained through cleanup. Deliberate double-free and VM errors are counted separately. Global before/after usage is observational, not a leak oracle. An unacknowledged release retains its exact diagnostic identity and blocks further checks.

slots.name: scheduler_kernel_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded scheduler/synchronization checks using the existing native cases on a BSP-only controller. Selection is a nonzero kernel_scheduler_check_case_* mask. Exact own task generations and work tickets remain resident until actual exit/release acknowledgments. Caller lifetime survives waits; close requests cooperative cancellation. Exclusive with native boot probes. No global reserve-failure injection, timer reprogramming or artificial clock advancement; those isolated cases are advertised separately. Returns 1 for a fixed report, 0 when unavailable, -1 for invalid selection/header/capacity without output mutation. Failed cleanup retains the resident session and prevents new work; never retry automatically.

slots.name: smp_kernel_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded functional SMP check on an owned BSP controller and one FPU-ready pinned worker per schedulable CPU. Reuses native placement/checksum, actual old/new mapping reads, exact request-generation remote TLB acknowledgments, monotonic clock and own heap/mutex contracts. Own task retirement precedes mapping/frame cleanup. No global DROP_ACK injection, global counter resets/empty baselines, speedup threshold, heap boot acceptance or R4L/serial boot assertions. Missing second CPU reports unavailable without work. Exact resources and failed releases remain resident; cooperative close cannot discard live workers or backing. Returns 1 for a fixed report including busy/failure/cancellation, 0 when context unavailable, -1 for invalid header/capacity unchanged output.

slots.name: performance_smp_tlb
slots.description: Passive current CPU/schedulable and clock-registration/quality snapshot plus actual remote TLB request/ACK/timeout counters since boot. Reports an active isolated injection explicitly; never starts work or presents historical boot outcomes as a new passing check. Loads are individually current, not atomic across owners; clock quality is functional even without detail metrics. Returns 1 for fixed snapshot, -1 for invalid version/capacity without output mutation.

slots.name: storage_block_queue_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded synthetic blockqueue diagnosis on an owned BSP controller. Shares existing independent-controller, bounded queue, reordered/duplicate completion, kill/unregister barrier, reset/late callback, real timeout/cancel, ordered flush and partial-batch cases. Uses own exact device/request/task generations, actual completion and retirement receipts; never touches physical test disks or resets global queues/counters. Failed resources remain resident and block another session. Returns1 for fixed report incl unavailable/busy/failure/cancel,0 for context unavailable,-1 for invalid header/capacity without output mutation.

slots.name: storage_nvme_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded read-only NVMe IRQ/completion proof. Binds one exact device generation and resident buffer through actual read completion and release. Matches native request/backend identity to a driver observation of its own hardware CQE, namespace/controller epochs and IRQ-driven worker pass after DMA release acknowledgment. Passive per-device before/after counters are descriptive only. Missing hardware/observation/IRQ capability is unavailable, not a pass. No deliberate write/reset/reconfiguration/fault injection. Caller output never reaches a worker; late or uncertain state retains resources/session. Returns1 for fixed report,0 for context unavailable,-1 for invalid header/capacity unchanged output.

slots.name: usb_contract_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded synthetic USB ring-cycle and event-router contracts using the existing native owner functions. Only private stack-local state; no allocation, waits, tasks, live mailbox access, real TRB submission, port reset or hardware reconfiguration. Reentrant and repeatable without USB hardware. This is not a physical USB/liveboot qualification. Returns1 for a fixed32-byte report,-1 for invalid header/capacity with output unchanged.

slots.name: serial_count
slots.description: Count currently registered ports, including reserved debug ports. Dynamic count, no two-port maximum.

slots.name: serial_port_at
slots.description: Copy one current port descriptor by catalog index;0success, NotFound at end. Enumeration is not an open reservation; use copied port_id+generation.

slots.name: serial_open
slots.description: Exclusively bind exact port generation to current process generation. Out handle zero on failure. Debug COM1 remains Busy until actual handoff.0success; provider open bounded/no retained buffers.

slots.name: serial_configure
slots.description: Configure exact process-owned open port; Busy until previous TX physically drains. Unsupported settings unchanged.

slots.name: serial_read
slots.description: Read_some raw bytes, wait for at least one only.0timeout polls. Finite logical-tick deadline, UINT64_MAX invalid. Per-port IRQ event wait leaves Ready list. Valid transfer output retains partial bytes/errors even on failure; no automatic replay. Empty call has no device effects.

slots.name: serial_write
slots.description: Queue raw bytes with exact accepted prefix; no framing.0timeout polls, finite ticks only. Per-port IRQ queue-space wait leaves Ready list. Partial bytes retained on timeout/cancel/error; caller keeps buffer through return. Physical completion requires drain.

slots.name: serial_drain
slots.description: Confirm empty software TX and actual hardware TEMT, not remote receipt. Finite ticks,0polls. IRQ readiness plus bounded timer for final shift completion; no yield spin.

slots.name: serial_status
slots.description: Coherent exact open-handle line/modem/buffer/error snapshot. No UART access through a reserved debug port.

slots.name: serial_cancel
slots.description: Cancel already admitted operations on this exact process-owned opening; wake only its serial waiters. Retain actual accepted bytes and device-owned buffers. Future operations may continue; no unrelated task/work completion signaled.

slots.name: serial_close
slots.description: Close admission, cancel/wake operations, await real callback references and hardware stop. Normal flags0 drains; serial_close_abort discards own queued bytes with accounting. Finite ticks;0polls. Timeout/unknown retains same closing handle and port/context for retry, successful0 alone releases ownership. Process/driver exit uses explicit abort with same actual quiescence.

slots.name: cpu_topology
slots.description: Copy one passive immutable boot CPU record. Returns cpu_topology_result_ok, _end, _invalid or _busy. Validate version1/caller capacity; errors and end leave output and any tail unchanged. No CPUID, allocation, wait, new hardware scan or hardware mutation during this query. Current online/schedulable flags are advisory per-call snapshots; calls across CPUs are not one transaction.

slots.name: cpu_cache_topology
slots.description: Copy one passive local cache descriptor for an exact boot CPU. Returns cpu_topology_result_ok, _end, _invalid or _busy; errors/end leave output and tail unchanged. Read CpuTopologyInfo cache_status to distinguish unavailable/invalid/truncated catalogs. No CPUID or new scan during this query.

slots.name: cpu_lifecycle
slots.description: Query0 is passive and requires expected_epoch0; any configured CPU including BSP is queryable. Offline1/online2 require the exact current nonzero epoch, BSP caller with IF on and no held owners, an admitted task, no concurrent CPU-sensitive probe, and a configured non-BSP target. Returns cpu_lifecycle_ok0, error_invalid/busy/index/epoch/context/qualification/state. Success writes exactly128 bytes and preserves caller tail. Every error leaves output unchanged; Busy may have moved safe saved tasks or IRQs and must be followed by query, never automatic retry. Before TLB withdrawal a rejected drain restores scheduling only after exact AP cancellation; after withdrawal uncertainty remains quarantined. Confirmed stop and fresh module baseline, CPUID, xstate, PAT, tables, LAPIC, clock and scheduler qualification are mandatory for reuse. No retained caller pointer, forced kernel-context migration, physical hotplug or CPU reservation.

slots.name: kernel_cpu_lifecycle_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded native CPU lifecycle work on an admitted BSP task with IF on and no owners. Returns1 for a fixed report (including Busy/failure/unavailable),0 when caller context unavailable, -1 invalid header/capacity with unchanged output. Exact task retirement and true hardware receipts govern success; retained resources block reuse. Leaves tested CPU freshly online after a successful cycle; never runs implicitly from metrics or boot.

slots.name: cpu_capabilities
slots.description: Passive CPU capture query. Returns cpu_capabilities_ok or error_invalid/index/busy. Any configured CPU including offline is observable; current lifecycle state is advisory. Only captured controls have validity flags. Unknown optional fields never block boot. Writes exactly272 bytes on success; every error leaves output and tail unchanged.

slots.name: cpu_feature
slots.description: Passive indexed query within CpuCapabilitiesInfo.feature_count for the exact nonzero current epoch; returns end after enumeration, error_epoch across reuse, busy during capture. Writes exactly112 bytes on success. Hardware, OS activation and unknown actual use are independent; raw data only when flagged. No output/tail changes on end/error.

slots.name: cpu_register_read
slots.description: Explicit named current-CPU read only. Returns cpu_capabilities_ok/error_invalid/index/busy/epoch/context/offline/unsupported/fault. Preserves caller IF and entire output/tail on failure. Caller routes through existing approved compute worker if needed; no general cross-CPU RPC or arbitrary MSR number. Architectural EFER/APIC_BASE/PAT/MTRRCAP require explicit capability; APERF/MPERF require exact Intel/AMD vendor and CPUID6.ECX0; Intel platform info limited to verified family6 models3C/45/46. Raw counters and nominal ratios are not current frequency. No public write. IF-on admitted task without held owners required at entry; refusal also preserves IF-off callers. Append-only CPUPOWER named IDs add proven Intel6:3C/45/46 sensor/energy reads and AMD19h:01h:B1 PPR reads. Named Intel microcode capture performs only the architectural zero-preload/CPUID1 latch; AMD patch8B never receives that write. No caller-controlled write or power request.

slots.name: kernel_cpu_register_check
slots.description: Explicit bounded local native instruction/#GP/IF check. Returns cpu_capabilities_ok with passed/failed report, or exact admission/header errors with unchanged output. IF-on task/no-held-owner context required at entry. Own membership lease prevents concurrent logical offline through final restoration. Exactly four fixed reserved-ID read/write probes; unsupported feature refuses before instruction. Writes exactly128 bytes; never implicitly runs in metrics/boot.

slots.name: cpu_power_info
slots.description: Passive cached external CPUPOWER observation. No register access, sampling worker, wait or policy write. Exact requested CPU epoch and provider instance; stale clock/CPU data lose valid bits. Returns cpu_capabilities_ok with explicit missing/unknown states, or exact header/index/epoch/busy errors preserving all output/tail.

slots.name: cpu_power_capture
slots.description: Explicit bounded local passive CPUPOWER capture. IF-on admitted task with no held owners, exact current CPU/start epoch and stable clock required. Caller routes via existing approved compute workers; no remote RPC or implicit wait. Reads never alter power requests/limits. Intel microcode signature may use its exact zero-preload/CPUID1 latch, AMD patch level is read only. Optional inaccessible values are reported unknown with raw/fault context. Returns cpu_capabilities_ok or exact errors with output/tail unchanged.

slots.name: cpu_performance
slots.description: Explicit local external performance provider operation with exact CPU/start/provider/ownership epochs. No governor or remote dispatch. Bad/unsupported requests preserve output and never write. Return0 provides the complete fixed receipt, including real fault/uncertain/conflict and reset-only activation; examine state/last_error and retain hardware until actual explicit release. Caller tail preserved. Request readback never claims physical delivered performance.

slots.name: cpu_cppc
slots.description: Explicit current-CPU external AMD CPPC operation. Abstract local request, separately consented one-way activation, exact baseline/token/revision and complete fault/readback receipt. Unsupported model/transport/epoch or invalid request performs no write. A return0 result supplies the receipt including uncertain/conflict; read state/last_error and retain hardware until actual local return. No governor, arbitrary MSR, physical frequency/energy or package-broadcast claim.

slots.name: cpu_performance_hint
slots.description: Passive cached same-catalogue preferred-core observation bound to exact CPU/provider/clock epochs and maximum1s sampling age. No model-register access, provider callback, work or policy. Missing/stale/incomparable observations are unknown, never low capacity or a placement guarantee. Refusal preserves caller output/tail.

slots.name: cpu_firmware_performance
slots.description: Explicit CPUPOWER firmware performance request, separately typed from local HWP/CPPC. May wait for actual external ACPIPLAT worker completion. Task/CPU/provider identities remain pinned; no Runtime/local-register owner spans the call. Refusal preserves output; complete receipt may report uncertain hardware and retained resources. No arbitrary model register, governor, automatic mutation retry or physical energy/clock claim.

slots.name: cpu_idle_info
slots.description: Passive copy of independent idle declaration, local qualification and software counters. Hardware residency, wake latency and energy remain unavailable without own readback; never execute CPUID/MSR/MONITOR on this query.

slots.name: cpu_machine_info
slots.description: Passive copy of bounded resident MCA boot/terminal receipt. No hardware work, lock, module callback or automatic retry. Error preserves output/tail.

slots.name: cpu_machine_bank
slots.description: Passive bank copy bound to exact CPU/original epoch/complete capture sequence. End or stale/busy/index/header error preserves all output/tail. Never arbitrary MSR access.

slots.name: cpu_microcode_info
slots.description: Passive fixed early microcode receipt. Exact CPU/execution epoch, real revision-read validity, loaded/supplied/virtual/prerequisite/failure states and post-baseline capture stay distinct. No update operation, hardware access or callback. Error preserves full output/tail.

slots.name: cpu_pmu_info
slots.description: Passive cached interface/model/current epoch and exact retained measurement ownership. No hardware access or callback.

slots.name: cpu_pmu_measure
slots.description: Explicit synchronous private CPU-counter scope, exact CPU/epoch/nonreused generation. Native supported named event only, virtual/unknown refused before MSR/work.1..4096 pure resident callback iterations, no allocation/fault/block/yield/API/placement call, IF0 only during short owned transaction then original IF. Original register state and exact readbacks before release; uncertain restoration retains quarantined PMU and lifecycle lease. Return0 means a complete receipt, not count validity; inspect status/flags. No arbitrary MSR/event/firmware interface. Work is a borrowed nullable pointer to one typed callback slot; null slot/address is invalid. SDK convenience facades pass a copied local function slot. No host-dependent optional-by-value callback enters the ABI.

slots.name: cpu_pmu_result
slots.description: Passive latest retained result copy for exact original CPU/epoch/generation. Offline/restart never relabel data; stale identity/error leaves all output/tail unchanged.

slots.name: cpu_acceleration_info
slots.description: Passive cached local optional CPU/OS facts and conservative all-configured hardware hints. No CPU instruction, measurement, callback or execution grant. Current CPU may change after return.

slots.name: cpu_acceleration_work
slots.description: Explicit synchronous pure resident baseline/SHA execution window. Exact TaskAdmission/lifecycle lease through output, original actual IF immediately before CLI, exact physical CPU/epoch/feature/OS revalidation. Virtual exposed ISA allowed, never PMU or physical qualification.1..64iterations,2ms accepted hardware clock. No allocation/fault/wait/yield/API/placement change; no Runtime owner across callback. No arbitrary feature mask/registers. Receipt0 alone not accepted: inspect flags/status/callback/identity/IF/clock. Refusal before work preserves output/tail; no automatic retry.

slots.name: fpu_observation
slots.description: Explicitly begin/end one current native task-generation/token/RIP-window observation. Scope records actual qualified local timer delivery, actual task switches and actual registered R4D hardware IRQ callbacks. No normal SysV call may be assumed to preserve XMM/YMM data. Direct IRQ guard calls do not count. Caller owns audited register-live bounds inside its retained module image. No caller pointer, lock or runtime borrow spans userland work; task retirement discards metadata, no hardware cleanup. Every failure preserves output and any existing observation. Zero events are unavailable hardware coverage.

slots.name: firmware_system_uuid
slots.description: Passive validated SMBIOS Type 1 system UUID in canonical RFC byte order. Returns 0 only for a nontrivial UUID; unavailable or invalid firmware preserves caller output. No network or storage side effects.

slots.name: device_inventory_capture
slots.description: Copy one complete passive device inventory into caller record storage in one existing collect traversal. Returns0 for a complete frozen copy; -2 reports insufficient capacity with generation0 and required_count, -3 refuses overflow, -4 refuses identity exhaustion. Existing per-source metadata copies are not globally atomic. No new scan, IO, allocation, persistent Kernel snapshot or device retain. Rows on any failure are private and must be discarded; receipt is valid on the documented capacity/overflow errors. All pointers are exclusively borrowed for the synchronous call; buffers must be mapped, aligned and disjoint. Null rows allowed only at capacity0. Actual return ends the loan; caller cancellation cannot forcibly end an active callback.

fields.name: memory_reserved_limit
fields.description: Profile reservation limit for explicit R4X VM-window virtual ranges, including SDK heap backing in that window; not the sum of all process VM ranges. Image and stack admission retain their separate bounds.

fields.name: memory_committed_limit
fields.description: Profile logical-commit limit for explicit R4X VM-window virtual ranges; a quota rather than current residency or history. Image and stack bounds remain separately enforced.

fields.name: memory_resident_limit
fields.description: Profile resident-admission limit for explicit R4X VM-window virtual ranges, including pending page-in admission. Pending frames are not actual resident bytes or resident high-water.

fields.name: memory_reserved_bytes
fields.description: Full-instance diagnostic: current sum of active VM-range reservations owned by this R4X instance, including image, SDK heap/explicit VM and main/secondary R4X stacks with reserved guards. Separately owned kernel/task stacks, shared R4L images and kernel payload/DMA allocations are excluded.

fields.name: memory_committed_bytes
fields.description: Full-instance diagnostic: current logical committed bytes on the same process-owned VM-range basis as memory_reserved_bytes; committed pages may be nonresident. This total has a broader basis than the explicit-VM-window profile quota.

fields.name: memory_resident_bytes
fields.description: Full-instance diagnostic: current simultaneously resident bytes over all active VM ranges owned by this R4X instance, including image, SDK heap/explicit VM and main/secondary R4X stacks. Separately owned kernel/task stacks, shared R4L images and kernel payload/DMA allocations are excluded. VM-range residency is not total physical RAM or unique-physical-page RSS.

fields.name: memory_peak_resident_bytes
fields.description: Historical maximum of the simultaneous memory_resident_bytes sum for this exact process generation, recorded at actual resident transitions even between status queries. It survives decommit, range release and instance reaping through the retained completion; a new generation starts fresh. Range peaks are neither added nor substituted. Saturates at u64 max. Lifecycle-only inventory omits memory diagnostics.

fields.name: stack_reserved_bytes
fields.description: Full-instance diagnostic: current main R4X stack VM-range reservation including its guard, from the same VM-owner snapshot as process totals. A subset of memory_reserved_bytes, not an additional charge. Secondary R4X stacks contribute to process totals but not this main-stack field.

fields.name: stack_committed_bytes
fields.description: Full-instance diagnostic: current logical committed bytes of the main R4X stack, including acknowledged stack growth, from the same VM-owner snapshot as process totals. A subset of memory_committed_bytes; neither the sum of secondary stacks nor necessarily resident bytes.

types.description: Full live-instance information reports coherent process-owned VM totals and the main-stack subset. A generation-bound retained completion preserves lifecycle data and memory_peak_resident_bytes; current memory/profile/stack fields are unavailable (zero placeholders) after the live instance row is retired. These placeholders must not be interpreted as measured zero usage. Lifecycle-only inventory requests omit all memory diagnostics.

fields.description: (GfxOwnedBufferReservation*, quiesced:u32) -> i32. Confirmed unwind only, also during closing Work/Shutdown; zero returns Busy without releasing ownership.

fields.name: buffer_take_release
fields.description: (adapter_id:u32, device_generation:u64, GfxOwnedBufferRelease*) -> i32. Actual driver, also closing. Busy if no matching pending resource. Claims one exact ticket after all consumers end.

fields.name: buffer_finish_release
fields.description: (GfxOwnedBufferRelease*, quiesced:u32) -> i32. Confirmed native unmap/free, also closing. Zero retains ticket/budget; stale, foreign or modified tickets cannot release backing.

fields.name: native_register
fields.description: (GfxNativeProvider*, GfxBufferHandle*) -> i32. Register actual Init/Work driver; writes handle on success only.

fields.name: native_unregister
fields.description: (GfxBufferHandle*) -> i32. Close provider, repeated busy until claims and callback completion drain.

fields.name: native_take
fields.description: (GfxBufferHandle*, GfxNativeJob*) -> i32. 1 claims oldest queued request; busy if none, closed after admission ends.

fields.name: native_complete
fields.description: (provider:GfxBufferHandle*, request:GfxBufferHandle*, result:i32, reference:GfxBufferHandle*) -> i32. Complete actual claimed allocation. For result=1 borrow a driver-owned canonical native BO reference; failures require zero reference. Outputs and driver reference remain unchanged. Late completion releases the claim without reviving cancelled work.

fields.name: memory_budget
fields.description: (const GfxDeviceBudgetRequest*, GfxDeviceBudgetState*) -> i32. Optional exact-owner query/configure; output unchanged on failure. No callback, allocation or wait under the BO metadata owner.

fields.name: telemetry_exchange
fields.description: (const GfxTelemetryState*, GfxTelemetryDemand*) -> i32. Optional exact-owner publication/demand exchange from Driver Work. No callback, allocation or wait. Old192-byte prefix is unchanged; output unchanged on failure.

fields.name: device_lost
fields.description: (adapter_id:u32, memory_generation:u64, quiesced:u32) -> i32. Optional exact-driver metadata invalidation of native BOs and closure of their device budget. quiesced=0 rejects new access while retaining physical storage; 1 additionally permits backing release after every device/queue lease retires, only with independently proven GPU/DMA stop. Existing public handles remain invalid but closable. CPU BOs and other generations are unaffected. No callback, allocation, hardware access or wait. Available during cached cleanup; the original 200-byte prefix and wire version 1 remain valid.

fields.name: virtual_register
fields.description: (GfxNativeProvider*, GfxBufferHandle*) -> i32. Register the actual driver for GPU virtual-memory resources. No competing hardware owner is created.

fields.name: virtual_unregister
fields.description: (GfxBufferHandle*) -> i32. Close admission and request retirement of every resource. Busy until claims, backend resources, borrowed BO references and notification work retire. Cleanup take/complete remain available.

fields.name: virtual_take
fields.description: (GfxBufferHandle*, GfxVirtualJob*) -> i32. Claim one ready operation; busy if none. Closing providers may take retirement jobs. The broker retains the canonical BO loan.

fields.name: virtual_complete
fields.description: (GfxBufferHandle*, GfxVirtualCompletion*) -> i32. Settle one exact claim. Unknown backend work must remain claimed until confirmed cleanup or reset. Success-only outputs and existing gfx-buffer result codes apply.

fields.name: reserved_span
fields.description: int32_t reserved_span(uint64_t physical_base, uint64_t bytes). Optional tail; 1 only for an aligned nonzero <=52-bit span fully covered by immutable boot reserved/framebuffer entries and no overlapping allocatable or reclaimable memory. Unknown gaps, conflicting entries and overflow fail. No allocation, mapping, RAM charge, ownership transfer or AMD-specific policy. Actual bound driver Init/Work owner; invalid=-1, unsupported=-6 using graphics buffer errors.

fields.name: unmanaged_span
fields.description: int32_t unmanaged_span(uint64_t physical_base, uint64_t bytes). Optional tail; 1 proves an aligned nonzero <=52-bit span overlaps no system memory in a complete, valid immutable boot map. Reserved/framebuffer entries and unlisted gaps are allowed; usable, reclaimable, kernel/module, ACPI, bad and unknown memory overlap fail. This is only a negative PMM/system-memory proof: the driver must independently measure actual device storage. It grants no device ownership, mapping, cache alias, allocation or RAM charge. Actual bound driver Init/Work owner; invalid=-1, unsupported=-6. reserved_span retains its stricter complete-coverage semantics.

types.description: DriverApi v25 owner-bound memory extension, optional owned-buffer tail after the original 112-byte prefix. Actual Init/ordinary Work context required; cached cleanup remains valid while closing. Outer DriverApi stays unchanged. Wire version stays 1. The 152-byte prefix is unchanged; the optional 184-byte tail exposes native allocation providers. The optional 240-byte tail adds owner-bound virtual-memory transport; the 208-byte prefix and wire version 1 stay unchanged. Optional reserved_span at 240 (table size 248) proves that a device storage carveout is outside all PMM-managed memory before a driver partitions it. Original 112/240-byte prefixes and outer DriverApi remain binary stable. Optional unmanaged_span at248 (table size256) separately proves exclusion from system memory even when UEFI omits a device carveout. The existing248-byte prefix, wire version1 and outer DriverApi remain binary stable; only the default caller capacity grows.

fields.name: size

fields.name: operation

types.description: Complete current512-byte copied bounded submission. No borrowed caller pointer survives Submit. Copy transports raw byte ranges; barrier orders dependencies; copy_rows uses logical offsets, per-row byte_length and checked pitches/extents. Render operation4 requires its explicit backend operation bit, zero copy offsets/length/pitches, optional source only for fill and a required target. The queue reserves canonical BO uses and copies all state. No CPU/GPU address or vendor command is accepted. Version1 remains current; historical short payloads are rejected without admission.

fields.name: flags
